question_text: Choose the option that correctly fills the blank: 'The committee members, along with the chairperson, _____ scheduled to meet tomorrow.'
explanation: 'Are' is correct. The subject is 'committee members' (plural). The phrase 'along with the chairperson' is an interrupter — it does not change the subject or the verb. Strip it out: 'The committee members … are scheduled.' 'Is' would be correct only if the subject were singular. 'Were' changes the tense to past, which contradicts 'tomorrow'. 'Has been' is present perfect singular — doubly wrong.

question_text: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error: 'He has been (A) working in this office (B) since five years (C) and has never (D) taken a day off.'
explanation: Parts A, B, and D are correct. 'Has been working' is correct present perfect continuous. 'In this office' is correct prepositional phrase. 'Has never taken' is correct. Part C is the error: 'since' marks a starting point in time (since 2019, since Monday), not a duration. A duration requires 'for' — 'for five years'. 'Since five years' is always wrong.
